iBooks on the iPad, 2010

Apple’s e-book app for the first iPad: a wooden bookshelf for the library and a bound book with stacked page edges for reading.

Source
Wikipedia: Apple Books
Creator
Apple
Made
Announced 27 January 2010 with the iPad
Style
Skeuomorphism (agent-proposed, not yet reviewed by a person)
Moods
Bookish, familiar, warm
Evidence
Inspected a 1280 px copy of File:1st-Gen-iPad-WiFi-iBooks.jpg (Evan-Amos, 2011, public-domain photograph of a first-generation iPad showing the iBooks reading view). The photo shows the reading view only. The bookshelf view is documented, not observed. Not stored.
Reviewed
28 September 2026
Rights
Link and metadata only. License: unverified. Rights policy

Context

Apple announced iBooks with the iPad on 27 January 2010. In Book layout, “pages are turned by tapping or dragging the page, animated to imitate the appearance of a paper book.” Wikipedia: Apple Books.

NN/g: “Ereaders, like iBooks and Kindle, were designed to look like physical bookshelves.” NN/g: Skeuomorphism.

On the day of the announcement, TechCrunch wrote that “the bookshelf view in iBooks is nearly identical to the main bookshelf view used in Delicious Library”; Wil Shipley noted that Mike Matas, a former Delicious Monster designer, worked on the iPad interface. TechCrunch, MG Siegler, 27 January 2010. See Delicious Library.

Observed

  • In landscape the screen shows two facing pages with a dark shadow in the gutter.
  • Thin stacked page edges run down the outer sides of both pages, as on a thick closed book block.
  • The pages are off-white; text is set in a serif face, justified and hyphenated.
  • A small bar at the top holds “Library” and table-of-contents buttons with a light bevel.

Why it belongs

The reading view carries non-functional detail from the physical book (page edges, gutter shadow) while the controls stay small and plain. It is a quieter case than the leather and felt apps.

Borrow

Suggest a long document with stacked edge lines at the sides instead of a scroll bar.

Put a soft vertical shadow in the gutter of a two-column reading layout.
